rationale: Turning the live-cluster statement recorded for the empty-configuration question from source-derived into measured. Every earlier measurement of that question used single-node clusters, so the discriminator asks what happens when the restarted node shares a cluster with a legitimate peer holding the correct configuration. A new focused probe (TestAssurance_LiveClusterEmptyConfigRestart) restarts one follower of a three-voter commit-tracked cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs, then measures (a) what the legitimate leader's continuing heartbeats do to the node's leader view, its configuration and its log, and (b) what one AppendEntries request from a sender that appears in no configuration does to the node, to the serving leader and to the cluster. A local dry run of the same file in the draft work copy produced the events this request expects: the restarted node held an empty configuration with no leader, converged on the serving leader as its heartbeats arrived and stored a command committed after the restart while its configuration stayed empty, and then accepted a higher-term AppendEntries from the sender that is in no configuration, adopted it as leader, raised its term, and the serving leader stepped down with no leader present afterwards. Those local observations are a construction check only; the receipt from this request is the evidence. No interpretation is restated or changed by this update.

scope.description: A three-voter in-memory cluster with a commit-tracking log store and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: the leader applies commands, one follower is shut down and restarted from its own stores on a fresh transport and reconnected, and the probe records the restarted node's recovered configuration and leader, what the legitimate leader's continued heartbeats do to the node's leader view, configuration and log, and what one AppendEntries request from a sender that appears in no configuration, carrying a higher term and no entries, does to the node, to the serving leader and to the cluster.
assumptions: Cluster, transport, log store and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.

Snapshotting is disabled by configuration and the recovered range is small, so the restarted node's configuration is empty rather than stale and NewRaft returns without the FSM batch blocking the parent question covers.
The outsider appears in no configuration the node holds and is wired to the restarted node's transport for the duration of the probe.
Timers are shortened to 200 ms so the observation window stays short.

experiment.prefix: Bootstrap three voters with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores, elect a leader and apply eight commands, shut one follower down and restart it with NewRaft on a fresh in-memory transport, reconnect the cluster, and emit the setup event with the configuration in force and the follower's staged commit index plus the restart-state event with the node's recovered configuration, state, term and leader. Poll until the legitimate leader's heartbeats reach the node, commit one command on the leader, and emit the convergence event with the node's leader, configuration length, state, whether it campaigned, and whether it stored the new command. Then wire a transport for a sender that is in no configuration, send one AppendEntries request with the node's term plus five, no entries and commit index zero, and emit the outsider event with the response, the node's term and leader afterwards, whether the serving leader stepped down and whether the cluster still has a leader.
experiment.requirement: A node that restarts with RestoreCommittedLogs inside a live cluster must not let a server outside the configuration it recovered change its term or its leader in a way that costs the cluster its serving leader.
experiment.responsibility: Raft itself: appendEntries decides whose leadership to record and which term to adopt, and the follower loop decides when the node campaigns from the configuration it recovered.

comparisons.description: The legitimate leader's heartbeats restore the restarted node's leader view.
Heartbeats and replicated entries leave the recovered configuration empty, so only an arriving configuration entry repairs it.
A sender that appears in no configuration does not become the restarted node's leader.
Contact with such a sender does not cost a healthy three-voter cluster its serving leader.
